column1: #mapping_set_title: HEAO mappings to HEO concepts, bridge axioms to OHEO and RHEO, and property correspondences

#mapping_set_description: Two tiers. Primary rows (mapping_tier primary) are exactly the bridge axioms of heao-bridge.ttl, written as the axiom reads, with the OHEO or RHEO class as subject and predicate rdfs:subClassOf or owl:disjointWith. Secondary rows (mapping_tier secondary) are in this file only. They are mappings from HEAO classes to HEO 1.3.0 concepts, which explain meanings, and correspondences between HEAO object properties and RHEO or OHEO properties, which differ in domain and so are not sub-properties. No row states identity and none uses skos:exactMatch. skos:closeMatch is used where the HEO concept and the HEAO class describe the same valuation idea, broad and narrow where one is a kind of the other, and related otherwise. In secondary rows the predicate reads from the HEAO subject. Every row carries the linking kind of the relationship as the CURIE of a HEAO individual, heao:4000001 definitional, heao:4000002 representational, heao:4000003 computational, heao:4000004 causal and heao:4000005 valuational. Convention for HEO rows. Close, broad and narrow matches are definitional. A related match is typed by the relation its reason states, computational where one is derived or calculated from the other, representational where one is the unit or the record of the other's result, definitional otherwise. Class rows to RHEO and OHEO record bridges withdrawn in the fix pass. owl:disjointWith is kept for the one disjointness bridge axiom, although it is not an SSSOM recommended predicate, so that the primary rows equal the bridge.

#comment: Written by src/build_heao.py and drafted by Michelle Ashley with Claude. Every row is proposed and unreviewed, so mapping_justification is semapv:UnspecifiedMatching; it becomes semapv:ManualMappingCuration with reviewer_id when a named curator signs a row off, and rejected rows are removed. reviewer_id and reviewer_label are left empty for that sign-off. Confidence is a house scale - 0.9 close match or bridge axiom, 0.8 broad, narrow or a strong related match, 0.7 related. Each reason states why the row holds and then quotes both definitions in full. Quoted HEO definitions are verbatim and may contain colons.

column22: comment

A QALY is the unit of the result of a health outcome valuation, not the valuation itself. HEAO defines health-adjusted time valuation as "A valuation in which time lived, or time spent in a health state, is converted into health-adjusted time on a health value scale, such as QALYs or DALYs, by applying a preference-based utility weight or a disability weight to each period."; HEO defines Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY) as "A quality-adjusted life year (QALY) combines length and quality of life in one measure: a year in full health counts as one QALY and death counts as zero.".

The HEAO method weights time by utility or disability weights; the HEO concept is the QALY case only, so it is narrower. HEAO defines health state weighting method as "A valuation method in which time is weighted by a preference-based utility weight or a disability weight for the health state it is spent in, and the weighted periods are summed."; HEO defines QALY Calculation Method as "The process of computing quality-adjusted life years by multiplying time spent in a health state by its utility value, then summing across states.".

A health-adjusted life year is a unit on a health value scale. HEAO defines health value scale as "A value scale on which health is expressed in units of healthy time, gained or lost, such as QALYs, DALYs or equity-weighted QALYs."; HEO defines Health-Adjusted Life Year as "A general term for outcome measures, including the QALY and DALY, combining length of life with a weighting for quality or disability into one unit.".

Both are the preference-based value of a health state used as a weight in economic evaluation. HEAO defines preference-based utility weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the preference for a health state on a scale on which full health is 1 and dead is 0, with values below 0 for states worse than dead, used to weight time lived in that state."; HEO defines Health State Utility Value as "A health state utility value, or HSU value, is a preference-based numerical weight assigned to a health state for use in economic evaluation.".

HEO's utility covers any numerical measure of preference, so the HEO concept is broader than HEAO's health utility used as a weight. HEAO defines preference-based utility weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the preference for a health state on a scale on which full health is 1 and dead is 0, with values below 0 for states worse than dead, used to weight time lived in that state."; HEO defines Utility as "Utility is a numerical measure of preference; in health economics, a health utility values a health state on a scale where 1 is full health and 0 is dead.".

Both are a loss of utility from a stated baseline, applied by subtraction. HEAO defines utility decrement as "A valuation weight that is a reduction in preference-based utility associated with an event, a treatment or a health state, applied by subtraction from a baseline utility."; HEO defines Disutility as "Disutility is the loss of utility caused by a health state, adverse event or treatment, measured from a stated baseline and used to reduce QALYs.".

A value set is one kind of weight function, the one that scores every state of a classification system. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines Value Set as "The complete collection of utility weights from a population valuation study, used to convert every combination of instrument responses into a utility score.".

An EQ-5D-3L value set is a weight function for every state of the EQ-5D-3L descriptive system. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines EQ-5D-3L Value Set as "EQ-5D-3L value sets are utility weights, elicited from a population's health state valuations, that score all 243 EQ-5D-3L states for QALY calculation.".

An EQ-5D-5L value set is a weight function for every state of the EQ-5D-5L descriptive system. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines EQ-5D-5L Value Set as "EQ-5D-5L value set is a scoring algorithm, estimated from a general public valuation study, that gives each of the 3,125 EQ-5D-5L states a QALY utility.".

A country value set is a weight function whose preference source is one country's population. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines Country-Specific Value Set as "A country-specific value set is a set of utility weights, elicited from one country's general public, that turns EQ-5D or similar responses into utilities.".

Capability index values are a weight function on the capability index scale, which cannot weight time in QALYs. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines Capability Index Values as "Capability index values are preference weights, often from best-worst scaling, that turn ICECAP answers into one score anchored at full and no capability.".

A multi-attribute utility is a value a multi-attribute weight function assigns. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines Multi-Attribute Utility as "A utility value derived by combining preference weights across several distinct attributes of an outcome into a single overall measure.".

Both apply a scoring algorithm from a prior valuation study to a respondent's answers. HEAO defines preference-based index scoring as "A health state scoring in which a person's health state profile on a preference-based measure is converted into a single utility by applying a value set, without the person valuing health states themselves."; HEO defines Indirect Utility Assessment as "The process of obtaining a health state utility value by applying a scoring algorithm from a prior valuation study to a respondent's questionnaire answers.".

Health state valuation in HEO is the elicitation and modelling that derives weights; HEAO's index scoring applies them. HEAO defines preference-based index scoring as "A health state scoring in which a person's health state profile on a preference-based measure is converted into a single utility by applying a value set, without the person valuing health states themselves."; HEO defines Health State Valuation as "Health state valuation is the elicitation and modelling of preferences for defined states of health to assign scores on a scale anchored by dead and full health for use in economic evaluation and related decisions.".

Preference elicitation derives the weights that valuation methods apply. HEAO defines valuation method as "A plan specification stating how values are obtained or applied in a valuation, such as valuing resources at market prices or at their opportunity cost, valuing lost work time by the human capital or friction cost method, or discounting at a constant rate."; HEO defines Preference Elicitation as "Preference elicitation measures what people value in health care from stated or revealed choices, yielding QALY weights, money values or risk trade-offs.".

The standard gamble is one way a preference-based utility weight is derived. HEAO defines preference-based utility weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the preference for a health state on a scale on which full health is 1 and dead is 0, with values below 0 for states worse than dead, used to weight time lived in that state."; HEO defines Standard Gamble as "The standard gamble is a choice-based health-state valuation method that finds the probability at which a respondent is indifferent between living in a certain health state and accepting a lottery between specified better and worse outcomes.".

The time trade-off is one way a preference-based utility weight is derived. HEAO defines preference-based utility weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the preference for a health state on a scale on which full health is 1 and dead is 0, with values below 0 for states worse than dead, used to weight time lived in that state."; HEO defines Time Trade-Off as "A health state valuation method asking how many years in full health a respondent would consider equal to a longer period in an impaired state.".

A visual analogue scale rating can be transformed into a utility weight, though it is not itself choice-based. HEAO defines preference-based utility weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the preference for a health state on a scale on which full health is 1 and dead is 0, with values below 0 for states worse than dead, used to weight time lived in that state."; HEO defines Visual Analogue Scale as "A health state valuation method in which respondents mark a perceived health state on a continuous line anchored between worst and best imaginable health.".

The person trade-off gives social values that can supply equity weights. HEAO defines equity weight as "A decision modifier QALY weight applied according to the group, condition or circumstance of the people who gain or lose, expressing a social value judgement about distribution rather than an individual's preference for a health state."; HEO defines Person Trade-Off as "Person trade-off (PTO) is a valuation method asking how many people helped one way equal a set number helped another, giving social values for health care.".

A discrete choice experiment can derive the coefficients of a weight function. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines Discrete Choice Experiment as "A discrete choice experiment, or DCE, presents respondents with repeated sets of hypothetical alternatives described by attributes and asks them to select a preferred option.".

Best-worst scaling can derive the weights of a weight function, such as capability index values. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines Best-Worst Scaling as "Best-worst scaling (BWS) is a stated preference method in which people pick the best and worst item in each set, to rank priorities or value health states.".

A mapping function predicts a utility for a health state from another instrument. Whether that prediction is a health state scoring is open for Darrin Baines, so the relation is only related. HEAO defines health state scoring as "A valuation in which a health state description, or a person's responses to an instrument, is given a weight on a weight scale, such as a preference-based utility or a capability index value, by applying a weight function."; HEO defines Mapping Function as "The specific statistical relationship, typically estimated through regression, used within a mapping algorithm to convert a health status score into a predicted utility value.".

A DALY is the unit of the result of a health outcome valuation by disability weights. HEAO defines health-adjusted time valuation as "A valuation in which time lived, or time spent in a health state, is converted into health-adjusted time on a health value scale, such as QALYs or DALYs, by applying a preference-based utility weight or a disability weight to each period."; HEO defines Disability-Adjusted Life Year as "The disability-adjusted life year (DALY) measures health loss by adding years of life lost to premature death and years lived with disability.".

DALY calculation weights years lived with disability by disability weights, the DALY case of health state weighting, so it is narrower. HEAO defines health state weighting method as "A valuation method in which time is weighted by a preference-based utility weight or a disability weight for the health state it is spent in, and the weighted periods are summed."; HEO defines DALY Calculation Method as "The methodology used to compute disability-adjusted life years, combining years of life lost to premature death with years lived with disability, weighted by severity.".

Both rate health loss in a state on a scale from 0, full health, to 1, equivalent to death. HEAO defines disability weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the loss of health in a health state on a scale on which 0 is full health and 1 is equivalent to death, used to weight time lived with disability in DALYs."; HEO defines Disability Weight as "A disability weight is a value from 0 (full health) to 1 (equivalent to death) rating health loss in a non-fatal state, used to calculate YLDs and DALYs.".

Years lived with disability are a result of weighting time with disability by disability weights. HEAO defines health-adjusted time valuation as "A valuation in which time lived, or time spent in a health state, is converted into health-adjusted time on a health value scale, such as QALYs or DALYs, by applying a preference-based utility weight or a disability weight to each period."; HEO defines Years Lived with Disability as "Years lived with disability (YLDs) measure non-fatal health loss, usually as prevalence times disability weight; adding years of life lost gives the DALY.".

Years of life lost value premature deaths against a standard life expectancy, the fatal part of a DALY valuation. HEAO defines health-adjusted time valuation as "A valuation in which time lived, or time spent in a health state, is converted into health-adjusted time on a health value scale, such as QALYs or DALYs, by applying a preference-based utility weight or a disability weight to each period."; HEO defines Years of Life Lost as "Years of life lost (YLL) measure premature mortality as deaths times standard remaining life expectancy at the age of death, the fatal part of the DALY.".

Health-adjusted life expectancy weights time by severity weights, a health outcome valuation at population level. HEAO defines health-adjusted time valuation as "A valuation in which time lived, or time spent in a health state, is converted into health-adjusted time on a health value scale, such as QALYs or DALYs, by applying a preference-based utility weight or a disability weight to each period."; HEO defines Hale Calculation as "The process of computing health-adjusted life expectancy, combining mortality data with health state prevalence and severity weights into one summary measure.".

Life years gained are time on a scale where every year has weight 1, the degenerate case that shows the weight is a choice. HEAO defines health value scale as "A value scale on which health is expressed in units of healthy time, gained or lost, such as QALYs, DALYs or equity-weighted QALYs."; HEO defines Life Years Gained as "Life years gained (LYG) are the extra years of mean survival an intervention gives over its comparator, without quality adjustment, in economic evaluation.".

HEO defines cost as the value of resources used, measured as the benefit forgone; that value is the result of a resource valuation, and when measured as health forgone it is the result of a health opportunity cost valuation. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Cost as "In health economics, cost is the value of resources used by a healthcare intervention, measured as the benefit forgone from their best alternative use.".

HEO's cost is measured as the benefit forgone from the best alternative use, which in health care is the health a health opportunity cost valuation estimates. HEAO defines health opportunity cost valuation as "A health-money exchange in which a cost falling on a constrained health budget is converted into the health expected to be forgone elsewhere in that system, by dividing it by a money value of a QALY taken to reflect the marginal productivity of the budget, either an estimated supply-side threshold value or a value a decision-making body has adopted for that purpose."; HEO defines Cost as "In health economics, cost is the value of resources used by a healthcare intervention, measured as the benefit forgone from their best alternative use.".

Both assign monetary values to measured resource use under a stated perspective and price year. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Cost Valuation as "Cost valuation is the assignment of monetary values to measured resource use in accordance with a specified perspective, setting, price year, and decision purpose.".

Cost measurement counts the resources that a resource valuation then values. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Cost Measurement as "Cost measurement is the step in economic evaluation that counts the resources each alternative uses, such as GP visits or bed-days, before they are valued.".

A direct cost is a result of valuing resources used for care. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Direct Cost as "Direct cost is a cost traced to a service or patient or, in economic evaluation, resources used for care or due to illness, such as medicines and travel.".

An intangible cost is a value that is hard to express in money, a contested resource or health valuation. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Intangible Cost as "A cost representing the non-financial burden of illness or treatment, such as pain or reduced quality of life, that is hard to value in money.".

Patient time cost values patients' hours at a wage or leisure rate, a resource valuation of time. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Patient Time Cost as "Patient time cost is the value of the hours patients spend travelling to, waiting for and receiving health care, often valued at a wage rate.".

An average cost is a unit cost on an average basis. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Average Cost as "Average cost is total cost divided by the number of units produced, such as patients treated or bed days, giving the cost per unit of a health service.".

A marginal cost is a unit cost on a marginal basis. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Marginal Cost as "Marginal cost is the change in total economic cost caused by producing one additional unit of output at a specified level of activity and over a specified time horizon.".

The marginal cost of healthcare is a unit cost on a marginal basis for one more unit of care. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Marginal Cost of Healthcare as "The additional cost of providing one more unit of healthcare service, such as treating one further patient.".

A capital cost spreads the value of an asset over its life, a resource valuation that uses discounting. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Capital Cost as "Capital Cost is the cost of assets used for over a year, such as buildings and medical equipment, spread over their useful life in economic evaluation.".

HEO's acquisition cost is the total a payer spends to buy a drug, which a price per unit multiplied by the quantity gives. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Acquisition Cost as "Acquisition cost is what a payer spends to buy a drug, at the price actually paid after any discounts, excluding administration and monitoring costs.".

An administration cost is valued with unit costs per administration. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Treatment Administration Cost as "Treatment administration cost is the cost of giving a medicine to a patient, such as nurse and chair time and consumables; it varies by route.".

An out-of-pocket cost is an amount paid by a patient, a valuation from the household's position. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Out-of-Pocket Cost as "The amount a patient or household pays directly for health care without third-party reimbursement, including applicable cost sharing and uncovered care.".

Micro-costing values each resource component with a unit cost, a resource valuation at item level. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Micro-Costing as "Micro-costing is a detailed method of estimating the cost of healthcare activities by identifying and measuring their individual resource components and valuing each component with an appropriate unit cost.".

Bottom-up costing multiplies each recorded item by its unit cost, a resource valuation. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Bottom-Up Costing as "Bottom-up costing estimates the cost of care by recording each patient's use of resources and multiplying every item by its unit cost.".

Top-down costing allocates aggregate costs, a resource valuation without a single unit cost. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Top-Down Costing as "A costing approach that starts with aggregate costs and allocates them to services, activities or patients using documented shares and output counts.".

Activity-based costing values activities by cost driver rates, a resource valuation. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Activity-Based Costing as "Activity-based costing (ABC) is a method that assigns resource costs to activities, then to patients or services in proportion to the activities they use.".

Time-driven activity-based costing multiplies time by a capacity cost rate, a unit cost of time. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing as "A costing method estimating a service's cost by multiplying the capacity cost rate of resources involved by the time required to complete each activity.".

Standard costing uses predetermined unit costs as weights. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Standard Costing as "A costing method that assigns predetermined, expected costs to services based on historical or engineered estimates rather than actual costs incurred.".

Cost allocation shares costs by a rule, a step in resource valuation. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Cost Allocation as "Cost allocation is the sharing of overhead and other indirect costs among health services or patients by a stated rule, such as bed-days or staff time.".

Common cost allocation divides a shared cost by a rule, a step in resource valuation. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Common Cost Allocation as "Common cost allocation is the division of a cost shared by several health services, such as overheads or a joint input, among them by a chosen rule.".

A cost-to-charge ratio converts a charge into a cost, a ratio applied to an amount already in money. HEAO defines monetary adjustment factor as "A valuation weight that is a ratio converting an amount of money from one price year or currency to another, such as a price index ratio, a market exchange rate or a purchasing power parity conversion factor."; HEO defines Cost-to-Charge Ratio as "The cost-to-charge ratio (CCR) is a hospital's reported costs divided by its billed charges, used to estimate costs from the charges on patient records.".

A price index ratio is formed from two values of a price index such as the consumer price index. HEAO defines price index ratio as "A monetary adjustment factor equal to the value of a price index in the target price year divided by its value in the original price year, used to inflate or deflate amounts of money."; HEO defines Consumer Price Index as "The consumer price index (CPI) measures change in the prices households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services, used to adjust costs for inflation.".

A shadow price is a unit cost on an opportunity cost basis where no market price reflects it. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Shadow Price as "The implicit value of a resource with no observable market price, reflecting the opportunity cost of using it in a particular way.".

HEO's opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone; the opportunity cost method values resources at it. HEAO defines opportunity cost method as "A valuation method in which a resource is valued at the value of its best alternative use forgone, including by a shadow price where no market price reflects that value."; HEO defines Opportunity Cost as "Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative given up when a resource is put to one use; in health care, usually health lost elsewhere.".

HEO notes that in health care opportunity cost is usually health lost elsewhere, which this valuation estimates. HEAO defines health opportunity cost valuation as "A health-money exchange in which a cost falling on a constrained health budget is converted into the health expected to be forgone elsewhere in that system, by dividing it by a money value of a QALY taken to reflect the marginal productivity of the budget, either an estimated supply-side threshold value or a value a decision-making body has adopted for that purpose."; HEO defines Opportunity Cost as "Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative given up when a resource is put to one use; in health care, usually health lost elsewhere.".

Both value lost productive time at earnings over the whole period lost. HEAO defines human capital method as "A valuation method in which productive time lost to ill health or premature death is valued at the earnings that would have been received over the whole period lost."; HEO defines Human Capital Approach as "A way to value productivity lost to illness or premature death by applying an economic value, often based on earnings, to forgone productive time.".

Both value lost production only over the friction period needed to restore it. HEAO defines friction cost method as "A valuation method in which productive time lost to ill health is valued only over the friction period needed to replace the absent worker and restore production."; HEO defines Friction Cost Method as "A productivity loss valuation approach estimating only the cost of the finite period needed to restore normal production, generally lower than human capital estimates.".

A diagnosis related group is the case group to which a payer's tariff assigns an amount. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Diagnosis Related Group as "A diagnosis related group (DRG) is a category of inpatient stays with similar diagnoses, procedures and expected costs, used to pay or fund hospitals.".

A case weight scales a tariff from a base rate, a relative weight applied in a payer valuation. HEAO defines valuation weight as "An information content entity that is a number applied in a valuation to convert a quantity into value, such as a utility, a unit cost, a discount factor, a money value of a QALY or an equity weight, stated with the value scale it converts to."; HEO defines Case Weight as "Case weight is a relative value for a diagnosis-related group showing its expected cost against the average case, used to scale payment from a base rate.".

A relative weight scales payment for a classification, a weight applied in a payer valuation. HEAO defines valuation weight as "An information content entity that is a number applied in a valuation to convert a quantity into value, such as a utility, a unit cost, a discount factor, a money value of a QALY or an equity weight, stated with the value scale it converts to."; HEO defines Relative Weight as "A numerical value assigned to a payment classification, such as a diagnosis-related group, reflecting its expected resource intensity relative to average.".

A relative value unit is a weight multiplied by a conversion factor to set a fee. HEAO defines valuation weight as "An information content entity that is a number applied in a valuation to convert a quantity into value, such as a utility, a unit cost, a discount factor, a money value of a QALY or an equity weight, stated with the value scale it converts to."; HEO defines Relative Value Unit as "A relative value unit is a standardized weight assigned to a covered service component to represent its relative resource use within the US Medicare Physician Fee Schedule.".

A resource-based relative value scale sets payer prices, an administered price method. HEAO defines administered price method as "A valuation method in which a resource or a care process is valued at the amount a payer has set for it in a tariff, a fee schedule or a price agreement, which may differ from both its market price and its opportunity cost."; HEO defines Resource-Based Relative Value as "A methodology determining physician reimbursement based on a standardised measure of resources required, incorporating work, practice expense, and malpractice risk.".

Fee-for-service pays by a fee schedule, a payer's valuation specification. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Fee-for-Service as "Fee-for-service is a provider-payment method in which each eligible health-care service generates a separate payment according to an applicable fee or contract.".

Case-based payment sets an amount per case group, a payer's valuation specification. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Case-Based Payment as "Case-Based Payment pays a hospital a fixed amount per treated case, set in advance for the case's group, often by diagnosis, not by the services used.".

A capitation rate is a payer's valuation per covered person. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Capitation Payment as "A capitation payment is a predetermined amount paid to a healthcare provider or organisation per covered person over a defined period for a specified set of services, largely independent of that person's actual service use.".

A bundled payment is a payer's price for an episode of care. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Bundled Payment as "Bundled payment pays a single price for all services in a defined episode of care, such as surgery and recovery, often spanning several providers.".

An ambulatory payment classification groups services that share one payer rate. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Ambulatory Payment Classification as "Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC) is Medicare's grouping of clinically similar, similarly costly hospital outpatient services sharing one base rate.".

A benchmark price is a payer-set reference amount, a payer valuation specification. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Benchmark Price as "Benchmark price is a payer-set reference amount, such as a Medicare Advantage or ACA benchmark, compared with bids, premiums or spending to set payment.".

Drug pricing sets the price a payer pays, recorded as a price agreement. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Drug Pricing as "The setting and negotiation of medicine prices and payments across a specified product, purchaser, market and point in the supply chain.".

An average manufacturer price can be the price basis of a unit cost weight for a medicine. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Average Manufacturer Price as "Average Manufacturer Price (AMP) is the average price paid to a manufacturer for a drug supplied to US retail pharmacies, the basis of Medicaid rebates.".

An average sales price can be the price basis of a unit cost weight for a medicine. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Average Sales Price as "Average sales price (ASP) is a manufacturer's average US price for a drug in a quarter, net of most discounts and rebates; it sets Medicare Part B payment.".

Best price is a pricing rule that sets a payer's rebate, a valuation specification. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Best Price as "Best price is the lowest US price a manufacturer offers almost any buyer for a brand-name drug in a quarter, used to set its Medicaid rebate.".

A confidential net price is a unit cost weight whose amount cannot be published. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Confidential Pricing as "Confidential pricing keeps a medicine's negotiated net price secret between manufacturer and payer, while a higher list price stays public.".

External reference pricing is a payer's rule for valuing a medicine from prices elsewhere, recorded as a RHEO international reference pricing rule. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines External Reference Pricing as "A medicine-pricing policy that uses prices for the same or comparable product in other jurisdictions as benchmarks for a domestic price or reimbursement decision.".

Differential pricing sets market-specific prices, payer valuation specifications that differ by market. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Differential Pricing as "Differential pricing is charging different prices for the same patented medicine in different markets, typically lower where ability to pay is lower.".

Cost-plus pricing derives a price from cost and a mark-up, a method of setting a price weight. HEAO defines valuation method as "A plan specification stating how values are obtained or applied in a valuation, such as valuing resources at market prices or at their opportunity cost, valuing lost work time by the human capital or friction cost method, or discounting at a constant rate."; HEO defines Cost-Plus Pricing as "Cost-plus pricing sets the price of a medicine or health product as its estimated unit cost plus a profit mark-up, either a percentage or a fixed amount.".

Cost-based pricing derives a price from costs and a margin, a method of setting a price weight. HEAO defines valuation method as "A plan specification stating how values are obtained or applied in a valuation, such as valuing resources at market prices or at their opportunity cost, valuing lost work time by the human capital or friction cost method, or discounting at a constant rate."; HEO defines Cost-Based Pricing as "Cost-based pricing sets the price of a medicine from its research and development, manufacturing, regulatory and overhead costs plus a profit margin.".

An equilibrium price is a market price, which the market price method applies. HEAO defines market price method as "A valuation method in which a resource is valued at the price paid for it in a market, such as a wage rate or a purchase price."; HEO defines Equilibrium Price as "An equilibrium price is the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied in a specified market under the model's stated conditions.".

A copayment is the patient's share set by a payer's rule. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Copayment as "A copayment (copay) is a fixed amount an insured person pays for a covered health service, such as USD 20 per visit, unlike percentage-based coinsurance.".

A cost-of-illness study aggregates valued resource use and lost productivity. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Cost-of-Illness Study as "A cost-of-illness study estimates the economic burden of a disease, including healthcare costs, patient and carer costs, and lost productivity.".

A bottom-up cost-of-illness study values patient-level resource use at unit costs. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Bottom-Up Cost-of-Illness as "Bottom-Up Cost-of-Illness estimates a disease's economic burden by valuing patient-level resource use at unit costs and scaling it to the population.".

Both are the cost of one unit of a good or service, such as a bed day. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Unit Cost as "The cost of producing or delivering a single unit of a good or service, such as the cost per hospital bed-day.".

Unit cost estimation produces the unit cost weight a resource valuation applies. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Unit Cost Estimation as "The process of determining the cost of delivering a single, standardised unit of a healthcare service, such as an inpatient bed-day.".

Both restate money from different periods in constant prices by a price index. HEAO defines price year adjustment as "A monetary revaluation in which an amount of money is moved from one price year to another by applying a price index ratio, as in inflating past unit costs to the price year of an analysis."; HEO defines Inflation Adjustment as "The process of restating cost data from different time periods in constant, comparable price terms, typically using a relevant price index.".

A price index ratio over one year is one plus the inflation rate of that index. HEAO defines price index ratio as "A monetary adjustment factor equal to the value of a price index in the target price year divided by its value in the original price year, used to inflate or deflate amounts of money."; HEO defines Inflation Rate as "The percentage rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services rises over a given period.".

A health price index supplies the values from which a price index ratio for health care is formed. HEAO defines price index ratio as "A monetary adjustment factor equal to the value of a price index in the target price year divided by its value in the original price year, used to inflate or deflate amounts of money."; HEO defines Health Price Index as "A measure tracking changes over time in the prices of healthcare goods and services specifically, unlike the general consumer price index.".

Both translate amounts from one currency into another by an exchange rate or purchasing power parity. HEAO defines currency conversion as "A monetary revaluation in which an amount of money is converted from one currency to another by applying a market exchange rate or a purchasing power parity conversion factor."; HEO defines Currency Conversion as "The translation of cost or price data from one national currency into another, typically using exchange rates or purchasing power parity.".

Purchasing power parity is the comparison method; the conversion factor is the number it supplies. HEAO defines purchasing power parity conversion factor as "A monetary adjustment factor equal to the number of units of a country's currency needed to buy the same quantity of goods and services in that country as one unit of a reference currency buys in the reference country."; HEO defines Purchasing Power Parity as "A method of comparing economic value across countries based on the relative cost of a common basket of goods and services, rather than exchange rates.".

Both convert costs across countries by purchasing power parity rather than exchange rates. HEAO defines purchasing power parity conversion as "A currency conversion in which a purchasing power parity conversion factor is applied, so that the converted amount buys the same quantity of goods and services in the target country as the original amount bought in the source country."; HEO defines Purchasing Power Adjustment as "The conversion of cost data across countries using purchasing power parity rather than market exchange rates, to reflect actual local costs.".

Both are the price of one currency in another, used to convert costs. HEAO defines market exchange rate as "A monetary adjustment factor equal to the number of units of one currency exchanged for one unit of another currency in a stated period."; HEO defines Exchange Rate as "The price of one currency expressed in terms of another, used to convert costs or prices between countries.".

A productivity cost is the result of a productivity cost valuation by the human capital or friction cost approach. HEAO defines productivity cost valuation as "A resource valuation in which time lost from paid or unpaid productive activity, or reduced output at work, because of ill health or premature death is converted into money, by the human capital method or the friction cost method."; HEO defines Productivity Cost as "The economic value of lost work output from illness or death, estimated using the human capital or friction cost approach.".

HEO's indirect cost includes lost productivity, which a productivity cost valuation values. HEAO defines productivity cost valuation as "A resource valuation in which time lost from paid or unpaid productive activity, or reduced output at work, because of ill health or premature death is converted into money, by the human capital method or the friction cost method."; HEO defines Indirect Cost as "A cost associated with an intervention that is not directly incurred in providing it, such as lost productivity from illness or premature death.".

A list price can be the price basis of a unit cost weight before discounts. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines List Price as "The publicly stated price a manufacturer offers a drug for sale, before accounting for negotiated discounts or rebates that reduce the price actually paid.".

A net price is the price basis of a unit cost weight after discounts. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Net Price as "The actual price a manufacturer realises for a treatment after all rebates and discounts, distinct from its publicly listed gross price.".

A price is what the market price method applies as a weight. HEAO defines market price method as "A valuation method in which a resource is valued at the price paid for it in a market, such as a wage rate or a purchase price."; HEO defines Price as "The amount of money required to purchase a good or service in a market transaction.".

Both convert future costs and health effects into present values. HEAO defines time valuation as "A valuation in which an amount of cost or health occurring at a stated time is converted into its present value at a base time by applying a discount factor derived from a discount rate."; HEO defines Discounting as "Discounting converts future costs and health effects, such as QALYs, into present values so that options with different timings can be compared.".

Both are the annual rate used to convert future costs and health outcomes into present values. HEAO defines discount rate as "A valuation parameter that is the rate per period by which the value of a future cost or health outcome is reduced for each period it lies beyond the base time, from which discount factors are derived."; HEO defines Discount Rate as "The discount rate is the annual rate, such as NICE's 3.5%, used in economic evaluation to convert future costs and health outcomes into present values.".

Both are the choice of different annual discount rates for health effects and for costs. HEAO defines differential discounting specification as "A discounting specification that states different annual discount rates for costs and for health effects."; HEO defines Differential Discounting as "Differential discounting applies a lower annual discount rate to future health effects, such as QALYs, than to future costs in an economic evaluation.".

HEO places hyperbolic discounting under time preference, a disposition; HEAO's class is the plan for deriving discount factors that falls continuously with delay. HEAO defines hyperbolic discounting method as "A non-constant rate discounting method in which the implied discount rate falls continuously as the delay grows, as with a discount factor of 1/(1+at) for a parameter a."; HEO defines Hyperbolic Discounting as "Hyperbolic discounting is time preference in which the discount rate falls as delay grows, so plans made for later are often reversed when the time comes.".

HEO defines hyperbolic discounting as a kind of time preference in which the rate falls as delay grows, so the HEO concept is narrower than HEAO's time preference. HEAO defines time preference as "A disposition of a person or a society to value a benefit less, or a cost less, the later it occurs, which a discount rate for health or for consumption may express."; HEO defines Hyperbolic Discounting as "Hyperbolic discounting is time preference in which the discount rate falls as delay grows, so plans made for later are often reversed when the time comes.".

A present value is the result of a time valuation. HEAO defines time valuation as "A valuation in which an amount of cost or health occurring at a stated time is converted into its present value at a base time by applying a discount factor derived from a discount rate."; HEO defines Present Value as "The current worth of a future sum of money or cash flow stream, found by discounting each future amount using a specified discount rate.".

A net present value sums the results of time valuations of a stream of flows. HEAO defines time valuation as "A valuation in which an amount of cost or health occurring at a stated time is converted into its present value at a base time by applying a discount factor derived from a discount rate."; HEO defines Net Present Value as "Net present value is the sum of monetary net flows at different times after each has been discounted to a common valuation date, including the initial flow.".

Both are the preference for benefits sooner and costs later that discounting expresses. HEAO defines time preference as "A disposition of a person or a society to value a benefit less, or a cost less, the later it occurs, which a discount rate for health or for consumption may express."; HEO defines Time Preference as "Time preference is the preference for benefits sooner and costs later; in health economics it is one reason future costs and QALYs are discounted.".

The time value of money is the principle that time valuation applies to money. HEAO defines time valuation as "A valuation in which an amount of cost or health occurring at a stated time is converted into its present value at a base time by applying a discount factor derived from a discount rate."; HEO defines Time Value of Money as "The principle that a given sum of money is worth more today than the same sum received in the future.".

An annuity payment spreads a price over years, whose present value is found by time valuation. HEAO defines time valuation as "A valuation in which an amount of cost or health occurring at a stated time is converted into its present value at a base time by applying a discount factor derived from a discount rate."; HEO defines Annuity Payment as "Annuity payment is an agreement to pay for a one-off therapy in yearly instalments, not upfront, with later ones sometimes stopping if the therapy fails.".

Discounting health is time valuation applied to health outcomes. HEAO defines time valuation as "A valuation in which an amount of cost or health occurring at a stated time is converted into its present value at a base time by applying a discount factor derived from a discount rate."; HEO defines Discounting Health as "The application of a discount rate to future health outcomes within an economic evaluation, converting them into a common present-day value.".

Discounting costs is time valuation applied to costs. HEAO defines time valuation as "A valuation in which an amount of cost or health occurring at a stated time is converted into its present value at a base time by applying a discount factor derived from a discount rate."; HEO defines Discounting Costs as "The application of a discount rate to future costs within an economic evaluation, converting them into a common present-day value.".

A social discount rate is a discount rate held by government or society. HEAO defines discount rate as "A valuation parameter that is the rate per period by which the value of a future cost or health outcome is reduced for each period it lies beyond the base time, from which discount factors are derived."; HEO defines Social Discount Rate as "The rate at which government or society as a whole is considered to discount future costs and benefits, used in public sector evaluation.".

A private discount rate is a discount rate held by an individual. HEAO defines discount rate as "A valuation parameter that is the rate per period by which the value of a future cost or health outcome is reduced for each period it lies beyond the base time, from which discount factors are derived."; HEO defines Private Discount Rate as "The rate at which an individual personally discounts future costs and benefits, typically higher than the social discount rate used in policy evaluation.".

Willingness to pay for a health gain or other benefit values that benefit in money as a whole, the result of a monetary benefit valuation. HEAO defines monetary benefit valuation as "A valuation in which a stated health benefit or other outcome is valued in money as a whole, such as by the willingness to pay elicited by contingent valuation, for use in cost-benefit analysis."; HEO defines Willingness to Pay as "Willingness to pay (WTP) is the most money a person would give up for a health gain or other benefit, used to value outcomes in cost-benefit analysis.".

Willingness to accept compensation values a loss in money as a whole, the result of a monetary benefit valuation. HEAO defines monetary benefit valuation as "A valuation in which a stated health benefit or other outcome is valued in money as a whole, such as by the willingness to pay elicited by contingent valuation, for use in cost-benefit analysis."; HEO defines Willingness to Accept as "The minimum compensation an individual would require to voluntarily give up a good or accept a worse outcome.".

Willingness-to-pay estimation derives the money values that a monetary benefit valuation records. HEAO defines monetary benefit valuation as "A valuation in which a stated health benefit or other outcome is valued in money as a whole, such as by the willingness to pay elicited by contingent valuation, for use in cost-benefit analysis."; HEO defines Willingness-to-Pay Estimation as "The empirical process of measuring willingness to pay, typically through stated preference methods such as contingent valuation or discrete choice experiments.".

Contingent valuation is the stated preference method by which a monetary benefit valuation usually derives its values. HEAO defines monetary benefit valuation as "A valuation in which a stated health benefit or other outcome is valued in money as a whole, such as by the willingness to pay elicited by contingent valuation, for use in cost-benefit analysis."; HEO defines Contingent Valuation as "Contingent valuation (CV) is a stated preference survey method asking people what they would pay for, or accept to give up, a described change in health.".

The contingent valuation method derives the money values of a monetary benefit valuation. HEO holds it beside contingent-valuation, a pair listed for merge review. HEAO defines monetary benefit valuation as "A valuation in which a stated health benefit or other outcome is valued in money as a whole, such as by the willingness to pay elicited by contingent valuation, for use in cost-benefit analysis."; HEO defines Contingent Valuation Method as "The contingent valuation method elicits a monetary value for a specified nonmarket health-related change by asking people what they would pay or accept in a carefully described hypothetical scenario.".

Monetary valuation expresses a health outcome in money, which a health-money exchange does when it applies the value. HEAO defines health-money exchange as "A valuation in which health is converted into money, or money into health, by applying a monetary value of health, as in the health term of net monetary benefit or the cost term of net health benefit."; HEO defines Monetary Valuation as "Monetary valuation expresses a health outcome or other non-market good in money terms, using stated preference, revealed preference or wellbeing methods.".

A value of a statistical life is a monetary value of a reduction in mortality risk. HEAO defines monetary value of health as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of health or of risk reduction, used to convert health into money or money into health."; HEO defines Value of Statistical Life as "A monetary estimate of the value society places on reducing the risk of death, derived from willingness to pay for a small risk reduction.".

A value of a statistical life year is a monetary value of one life year. HEAO defines monetary value of health as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of health or of risk reduction, used to convert health into money or money into health."; HEO defines Value of Statistical Life Year as "An adaptation of the value of statistical life expressed per life-year rather than per life, adjusted for age and remaining life expectancy.".

Benefit transfer reuses a monetary value of health in a new context, a change of valuation context that HEAO records. HEAO defines monetary value of health as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of health or of risk reduction, used to convert health into money or money into health."; HEO defines Benefit Transfer as "Benefit transfer reuses willingness-to-pay values from earlier studies, such as the value of a statistical life, to value health benefits in a new setting.".

HEO's willingness-to-pay threshold is, strictly, the most society would pay for one QALY, a demand-side money value of a QALY. HEAO defines consumption value of a QALY as "A money value of a QALY estimated from the demand side, as the amount of consumption that individuals or society are willing to give up for one QALY."; HEO defines Willingness-to-Pay Threshold as "A willingness-to-pay threshold is the cost per QALY below which a treatment counts as good value; strictly, the most society would pay for one extra QALY.".

HEO's cost-effectiveness threshold is the maximum cost per QALY a health system treats as value for money, the figure a body adopts, which is this weight when applied. HEAO defines adopted threshold value as "A money value of a QALY adopted by a decision-making body in a decision threshold specification, for comparison with incremental cost-effectiveness ratios and for net benefit, whatever basis it is meant to reflect, such as the £25,000 to £35,000 per QALY that NICE adopts and intends to reflect the opportunity cost of programmes displaced."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness Threshold as "A cost-effectiveness threshold is the maximum cost per QALY gained that a health system treats as value for money when deciding which treatments to fund.".

The NICE threshold is the range NICE adopts in PMG36 sections 6.3.4 to 6.3.8, stated in a decision threshold specification whose number is an adopted threshold value. HEAO defines adopted threshold value as "A money value of a QALY adopted by a decision-making body in a decision threshold specification, for comparison with incremental cost-effectiveness ratios and for net benefit, whatever basis it is meant to reflect, such as the £25,000 to £35,000 per QALY that NICE adopts and intends to reflect the opportunity cost of programmes displaced."; HEO defines NICE Threshold as "The NICE threshold is the £25,000 to £35,000 per QALY gained range NICE committees use to judge whether an ICER is an effective use of NHS resources.".

The shadow price of health is the value of health forgone at the margin, which an estimated supply-side threshold value measures. HEAO defines estimated supply-side threshold value as "A money value of a QALY estimated from the supply side, as the cost at which a health system is expected to give up one QALY elsewhere when its budget is displaced, from evidence on the marginal productivity of its spending."; HEO defines Shadow Price of Health as "The implicit value of health gains forgone when a health budget is spent inefficiently, used as a basis for setting a cost-effectiveness threshold.".

The shadow price of the budget is the health forgone per unit of money, the reciprocal of an estimated supply-side threshold value. HEAO defines estimated supply-side threshold value as "A money value of a QALY estimated from the supply side, as the cost at which a health system is expected to give up one QALY elsewhere when its budget is displaced, from evidence on the marginal productivity of its spending."; HEO defines Shadow Price of Budget as "The implicit value of relaxing a fixed health budget by one extra unit of currency, reflecting the health forgone elsewhere if it is not spent optimally.".

Net monetary benefit values health in money at a threshold and subtracts cost; the multiplication is a health-money exchange. HEAO defines health-money exchange as "A valuation in which health is converted into money, or money into health, by applying a monetary value of health, as in the health term of net monetary benefit or the cost term of net health benefit."; HEO defines Net Monetary Benefit as "Net monetary benefit (NMB) is an option's health outcome valued in money at a cost-effectiveness threshold minus its cost, used to rank healthcare options.".

Incremental net monetary benefit values the extra health in money, a health-money exchange, then subtracts the extra cost. HEAO defines health-money exchange as "A valuation in which health is converted into money, or money into health, by applying a monetary value of health, as in the health term of net monetary benefit or the cost term of net health benefit."; HEO defines Incremental Net Monetary Benefit as "Incremental net monetary benefit (INMB) is the extra health of an option over its comparator, valued at a threshold, minus the extra cost, per patient.".

Net health benefit subtracts the QALYs an extra cost would buy elsewhere, which a health opportunity cost valuation estimates. HEAO defines health opportunity cost valuation as "A health-money exchange in which a cost falling on a constrained health budget is converted into the health expected to be forgone elsewhere in that system, by dividing it by a money value of a QALY taken to reflect the marginal productivity of the budget, either an estimated supply-side threshold value or a value a decision-making body has adopted for that purpose."; HEO defines Net Health Benefit as "Net health benefit (NHB) is the health an option gains, in QALYs, minus the QALYs its extra cost would buy elsewhere at the cost-effectiveness threshold.".

Net benefit places health and costs on one scale, the result of the net benefit method. HEAO defines net benefit method as "A valuation method in which health and costs are placed on one scale by valuing health at a stated money value of health, or costs at the health they would buy, so that options are compared by net benefit."; HEO defines Net Benefit as "Net benefit places health gains and costs on one scale by valuing health at a cost-effectiveness threshold, or directly in money, and subtracting costs.".

Incremental net benefit is a difference of net benefits obtained by the net benefit method. HEAO defines net benefit method as "A valuation method in which health and costs are placed on one scale by valuing health at a stated money value of health, or costs at the health they would buy, so that options are compared by net benefit."; HEO defines Incremental Net Benefit as "The difference in expected net benefit between two competing interventions, found by converting the incremental health effect into money and subtracting incremental cost.".

Both rank options by net benefit at a stated threshold instead of by ratios. HEAO defines net benefit method as "A valuation method in which health and costs are placed on one scale by valuing health at a stated money value of health, or costs at the health they would buy, so that options are compared by net benefit."; HEO defines Net Benefit Approach as "The net benefit approach is a cost-effectiveness decision framework that ranks options by net benefit at a stated threshold instead of by ratios.".

Expected net benefit across parameter uncertainty is the input from which value of information is calculated. HEAO defines value of information analysis as "A valuation in which the expected value of reducing decision uncertainty is assigned, as the expected gain in net benefit from deciding with more information, calculated from a probabilistic analysis at a stated money value of health."; HEO defines Expected Net Benefit as "Expected net benefit is the mean net benefit of a healthcare option across parameter uncertainty at a set threshold; the option with the highest is chosen.".

A threshold price follows from valuing a technology's health gain at a threshold. HEAO defines health-money exchange as "A valuation in which health is converted into money, or money into health, by applying a monetary value of health, as in the health term of net monetary benefit or the cost term of net health benefit."; HEO defines Threshold Price as "Threshold Price is the highest price at which a health technology stays cost-effective: the price where its ICER equals the cost-effectiveness threshold.".

An economically justifiable price follows from valuing health at a payer's threshold. HEAO defines health-money exchange as "A valuation in which health is converted into money, or money into health, by applying a monetary value of health, as in the health term of net monetary benefit or the cost term of net health benefit."; HEO defines Economically Justifiable Price as "The economically justifiable price (EJP) is the top price a manufacturer can defend on cost-effectiveness grounds at a given payer's threshold.".

Value-based pricing is a rule setting price from the health added valued at a threshold. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Value-Based Pricing as "Value-based pricing sets a medicine's price by the health it adds over current care, typically the highest price that meets a cost-effectiveness threshold.".

A benefit-cost ratio divides monetised benefits, the results of health-money exchanges, by costs. HEAO defines health-money exchange as "A valuation in which health is converted into money, or money into health, by applying a monetary value of health, as in the health term of net monetary benefit or the cost term of net health benefit."; HEO defines Benefit-Cost Ratio as "Benefit-cost ratio (BCR) is a health programme's monetised benefits divided by its costs, in present values, used to summarise a cost-benefit analysis.".

Cost-benefit analysis values costs and benefits in money and compares them by net benefit. HEAO defines net benefit method as "A valuation method in which health and costs are placed on one scale by valuing health at a stated money value of health, or costs at the health they would buy, so that options are compared by net benefit."; HEO defines Cost-Benefit Analysis as "Cost-benefit analysis values the costs and benefits of healthcare options in money, so they can be compared by their net benefit, usually to society.".

An affordability threshold is a budget rule, a decision maker's specification that is not a value of health. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Affordability Threshold as "An affordability threshold is the budget impact level above which a payer flags a new technology for special handling, even if it is cost-effective.".

A cost-effectiveness acceptability curve shows results across a range of money values of a QALY. HEAO defines money value of a QALY as "A monetary value of health that is an amount of money per QALY, used as the exchange rate between health and money in net benefit and in comparison with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Curve (CEAC) as "A cost-effectiveness acceptability curve (CEAC) plots, across cost-effectiveness thresholds, the probability that each option is the most cost-effective.".

A decision rule states the criterion, such as a threshold, against which results are judged. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Decision Rule as "A decision rule is an explicit criterion, such as an ICER threshold or net benefit, for choosing between healthcare interventions in economic evaluation.".

HEO names the whole analysis in which health gains for priority groups are weighted more heavily; HEAO's class is the valuation step within it, a part of the whole. HEAO defines equity weighting as "A decision modifier weighting in which health or money already valued is weighted by an equity weight, or aggregated with an inequality aversion parameter, to express a social value judgement about whose gains or losses count for more."; HEO defines Equity-Weighted Analysis as "Equity-weighted analysis is a cost-effectiveness analysis in which health gains for priority groups, such as the severely ill, are weighted more heavily.".

Distributional cost-effectiveness analysis can aggregate health with an inequality aversion parameter, a nonlinear equity weighting.
