HEAO defines equity weighting as "A decision modifier weighting in which health or money already valued is weighted by an equity weight, or aggregated with an inequality aversion parameter, to express a social value judgement about whose gains or losses count for more."; HEO defines Distributional Cost-Effectiveness as "Distributional cost-effectiveness analysis (DCEA) is an economic evaluation showing who gains and loses health from a policy and its effect on inequality.".

QALY shortfall measures the severity that decides a severity weight. HEAO defines severity weighting as "An equity weighting in which QALYs gained are weighted according to the severity of the condition, measured by absolute or proportional QALY shortfall, under a severity weighting rule."; HEO defines QALY Shortfall as "QALY shortfall is the expected QALY gap between a matched general population and patients on current care, which NICE reads as absolute or proportional.".

Absolute shortfall is one of the two measures that decide a severity weight. HEAO defines severity weighting as "An equity weighting in which QALYs gained are weighted according to the severity of the condition, measured by absolute or proportional QALY shortfall, under a severity weighting rule."; HEO defines Absolute Shortfall as "Absolute shortfall is the future QALYs lost with a condition under current care versus the age- and sex-matched population, used by NICE to judge severity.".

Proportional shortfall is one of the two measures that decide a severity weight. HEAO defines severity weighting as "An equity weighting in which QALYs gained are weighted according to the severity of the condition, measured by absolute or proportional QALY shortfall, under a severity weighting rule."; HEO defines Proportional Shortfall as "A measure of disease severity calculated as the proportion, rather than absolute number, of expected quality-adjusted life years lost to a condition.".

The Atkinson index uses an explicit inequality aversion parameter. HEAO defines inequality aversion parameter as "A valuation parameter expressing how much total health a social decision maker would give up for a more equal distribution, as in the Atkinson index and the equally distributed equivalent."; HEO defines Atkinson Index as "The Atkinson index measures inequality in health or income using a social welfare function with an explicit inequality aversion parameter, epsilon.".

A social welfare function sets how equality is weighed against the total, the basis of nonlinear equity weighting. HEAO defines equity weighting method as "A valuation method stating how equity concerns enter a valuation, such as multiplying health gains by group weights or aggregating health with an inequality aversion parameter."; HEO defines Social Welfare Function as "A social welfare function (SWF) combines individual health or wellbeing into overall social welfare, setting how equality is weighed against the total.".

The inequality aversion parameter states how much total health is given up for a fairer distribution. HEAO defines inequality aversion parameter as "A valuation parameter expressing how much total health a social decision maker would give up for a more equal distribution, as in the Atkinson index and the equally distributed equivalent."; HEO defines Equity-Efficiency Trade-off as "The equity-efficiency trade-off is the total health given up for a fairer distribution when the option that maximises health is not the fairest one.".

Age weighting values healthy years by the age they are lived at, an equity weight by age. HEAO defines equity weight as "A decision modifier QALY weight applied according to the group, condition or circumstance of the people who gain or lose, expressing a social value judgement about distribution rather than an individual's preference for a health state."; HEO defines Age Weighting as "Age weighting values a year of healthy life by the age at which it is lived, as in the original GBD DALY, which gave years in young adulthood most weight.".

Extended cost-effectiveness analysis adds distributional results, an equity concern handled outside a single weight. HEAO defines equity weighting method as "A valuation method stating how equity concerns enter a valuation, such as multiplying health gains by group weights or aggregating health with an inequality aversion parameter."; HEO defines Extended Cost-Effectiveness as "A form of economic evaluation that extends standard cost-effectiveness analysis by incorporating financial risk protection and the distribution of costs and benefits by income.".

Both are NICE's rule giving QALY weights of 1.2 or 1.7 by absolute or proportional QALY shortfall, as PMG36 table 6.1 states. HEAO defines severity weighting rule as "An equity weighting rule that sets the weight given to QALYs by bands of absolute and proportional QALY shortfall, applying whichever implies the greater severity."; HEO defines Severity Modifier as "The severity modifier is a weight of 1.2 or 1.7 that NICE applies to QALY gains for conditions with a high absolute or proportional QALY shortfall.".

The weights 1.2 and 1.7 that the severity modifier sets are severity weights. HEAO defines severity weight as "An equity weight applied to QALYs according to the severity of the condition, as measured by absolute or proportional QALY shortfall, such as the QALY weights of 1.2 and 1.7 in table 6.1 of the NICE manual."; HEO defines Severity Modifier as "The severity modifier is a weight of 1.2 or 1.7 that NICE applies to QALY gains for conditions with a high absolute or proportional QALY shortfall.".

A severity criterion gives extra weight to more severe conditions, the basis of an equity weighting rule. HEAO defines equity weighting rule as "A decision modifier rule stating which groups, conditions or circumstances receive which equity weight, and the criteria that decide it."; HEO defines Severity Criterion as "A standard giving additional weight to interventions addressing more severe conditions, reflecting a preference for prioritising the greatest health shortfall.".

Both estimate the expected benefit of reducing decision uncertainty. HEAO defines value of information analysis as "A valuation in which the expected value of reducing decision uncertainty is assigned, as the expected gain in net benefit from deciding with more information, calculated from a probabilistic analysis at a stated money value of health."; HEO defines Value of Information as "Value of information (VOI) analysis estimates the expected benefit of reducing decision uncertainty, to judge whether more research is worth its cost.".

Both are the expected gain from removing all uncertainty in a decision, the upper limit on the value of research. HEAO defines EVPI estimate as "A value of information estimate of the expected gain in net benefit per person from resolving all uncertainty in the parameters of a decision model before choosing, equal to the expected value of the maximum net benefit across options minus the maximum of the expected net benefits."; HEO defines Expected Value of Perfect Information as "Expected value of perfect information (EVPI) is the expected gain from removing all uncertainty in a funding decision, the upper limit on research value.".

column8: Expected Value of Partial Perfect Information
column22: Both are the expected gain in net benefit from knowing selected parameters exactly before deciding. HEAO defines EVPPI estimate as "A value of information estimate of the expected gain in net benefit per person from resolving the uncertainty in a stated subset of parameters before choosing, with the uncertainty in the other parameters left unresolved."; HEO defines Expected Value of Partial Perfect Information as "Expected value of partial perfect information (EVPPI) is the expected gain in net benefit from knowing selected model parameters exactly before deciding.".

Both are the expected gain from deciding after a specific study reports. HEAO defines EVSI estimate as "A value of information estimate of the expected gain in net benefit per person from deciding after a study of stated design and sample size reports."; HEO defines Expected Value of Sample Information as "Expected value of sample information (EVSI) is the expected net benefit gained by deciding after a specific proposed study reports instead of deciding now.".

Both scale the EVPI per person to the population affected by the decision over its lifetime. HEAO defines population EVPI estimate as "A value of information estimate equal to the EVPI per person multiplied by the discounted number of people expected to be affected by the decision over its expected lifetime, which bounds the value of further research on that decision."; HEO defines Population EVPI as "The expected value of perfect information calculated for an entire affected patient population over time, rather than for a single patient.".

Both are a proposed study's population EVSI minus its expected cost. HEAO defines ENBS estimate as "A value of information estimate equal to the population EVSI of a proposed study minus the expected cost of the study, which is maximised over sample sizes and allocations to choose the design of further research."; HEO defines Expected Net Benefit of Sampling as "Expected net benefit of sampling (ENBS) is a proposed study's population expected value of sample information minus its expected total cost.".

HEO's perspective decides which costs and outcomes are counted, the analytic perspective; the valuation perspective is whose values supply the weights, so the two are related, not the same. HEAO defines valuation perspective as "A directive information entity stating whose values supply the weights a valuation applies, such as the preferences of a general population or of patients, the prices a payer pays, or the social value judgements of a decision-making body."; HEO defines Perspective as "Perspective in health economic evaluation is the viewpoint, such as the health system, payer or society, that decides which costs and outcomes are counted.".

A societal perspective is an analytic perspective; its valuation perspective may still be a payer's prices or a population's preferences. HEAO defines valuation perspective as "A directive information entity stating whose values supply the weights a valuation applies, such as the preferences of a general population or of patients, the prices a payer pays, or the social value judgements of a decision-making body."; HEO defines Societal Perspective as "The societal perspective is an economic evaluation viewpoint that counts all costs and outcomes, whoever bears them, including productivity and carer time.".

HEO's payer perspective counts a payer's costs; the payer valuation perspective values resources at the payer's prices. HEAO defines payer valuation perspective as "A valuation perspective in which resources are valued at the amounts a stated payer pays for them, through tariffs, fee schedules or price agreements."; HEO defines Payer Perspective as "An analytic viewpoint including only costs and outcomes relevant to a specific healthcare payer, such as an insurer or government health programme.".

A reference case is a set of methods a valuation context can name. HEAO defines valuation context as "An information content entity stating the setting for which a valuation is made, namely the jurisdiction, the decision maker, the decision problem, the currency and price year, the reference case claimed and the date, against which the appropriateness of its weights and perspective can be judged."; HEO defines Reference Case as "A reference case is the set of methods, such as perspective, outcome measure and discounting, that HTA bodies like NICE expect economic evaluations to use.".

Both assign a monetary value to a measured quantity of resource use, typically a quantity multiplied by a unit cost. HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method."; HEO defines Resource Valuation as "The process of assigning a monetary value to a measured quantity of resource use, typically by multiplying it by a unit cost.".

Both reduce future costs and benefits at a constant proportional rate each period. HEAO defines constant rate discounting method as "A discounting method in which the discount factor for an amount t years after the base time is 1/(1+r)^t, for a constant annual discount rate r."; HEO defines Exponential Discounting as "A discounting model in which future costs and benefits are reduced at a constant proportional rate each period, producing time-consistent preferences.".

Both estimate the value of reducing decision uncertainty from a probabilistic analysis. HEO holds voi-analysis beside value-of-information, a pair for HEO merge review. HEAO defines value of information analysis as "A valuation in which the expected value of reducing decision uncertainty is assigned, as the expected gain in net benefit from deciding with more information, calculated from a probabilistic analysis at a stated money value of health."; HEO defines VOI Analysis as "VOI analysis (value of information analysis) takes a model's PSA through EVPI, EVPPI, EVSI and ENBS in turn to decide if more research is worth its cost.".

HEO's preference weight is a value of the desirability of a health state or outcome, the source of a preference-based utility weight. OHEO's preference weight, a value set coefficient, has a narrower meaning. HEAO defines preference-based utility weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the preference for a health state on a scale on which full health is 1 and dead is 0, with values below 0 for states worse than dead, used to weight time lived in that state."; HEO defines Preference Weight as "A numerical value reflecting the relative desirability a population or individual assigns to a particular health state or outcome.".

Discount rate selection is the decision that fixes the discount rate a discounting specification states. HEAO defines discount rate as "A valuation parameter that is the rate per period by which the value of a future cost or health outcome is reduced for each period it lies beyond the base time, from which discount factors are derived."; HEO defines Discount Rate Selection as "The methodological decision on which discount rate to apply in an economic evaluation, informed by the social opportunity cost of capital and relevant guidance.".

Present bias is a pattern of time preference stronger than constant discounting predicts. HEAO defines time preference as "A disposition of a person or a society to value a benefit less, or a cost less, the later it occurs, which a discount rate for health or for consumption may express."; HEO defines Present Bias as "The tendency to place disproportionate weight on immediate rewards or costs relative to future ones, beyond what constant discounting predicts.".

A future value compounds a present amount forward, the inverse of the present value a time valuation gives. HEAO defines time valuation as "A valuation in which an amount of cost or health occurring at a stated time is converted into its present value at a base time by applying a discount factor derived from a discount rate."; HEO defines Future Value as "The value a present sum of money will grow to after a specified period, given a particular rate of return.".

column8: Equal Value of Life Year Gained
column22: Equal value life years gained are counted on a health value scale on which every added year has the same weight. HEAO defines health value scale as "A value scale on which health is expressed in units of healthy time, gained or lost, such as QALYs, DALYs or equity-weighted QALYs."; HEO defines Equal Value of Life Year Gained as "An alternative to the QALY that values every extra year of life gained equally, regardless of the quality of life experienced during it.".

HEO's utility function assigns a number to each outcome; OHEO's utility function, bridged under weight function, is the HEAO counterpart. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines Utility Function as "A mathematical representation of preferences that assigns a numerical value to each possible outcome, so higher-utility outcomes are preferred.".

Value set development is the study that produces a value set, a weight function. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines Value Set Development as "The process of designing, conducting, and analysing a population valuation study to produce a scoring algorithm for a health status instrument.".

Part-worth utilities from a choice experiment can be the coefficients of a weight function. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines Part-Worth Utility as "The contribution of a single attribute level to an individual's overall utility for a good, estimated from a conjoint or choice experiment.".

A single attribute utility is a value given by a single-attribute utility function, a kind of weight function. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines Single Attribute Utility as "A utility value derived from a single dimension of health or outcome, unlike multi-attribute utility, which integrates several dimensions.".

Stated preference methods supply the money values a monetary benefit valuation applies. HEAO defines monetary benefit valuation as "A valuation in which a stated health benefit or other outcome is valued in money as a whole, such as by the willingness to pay elicited by contingent valuation, for use in cost-benefit analysis."; HEO defines Stated Preference as "A category of valuation methods that elicits preferences by asking people directly about hypothetical choices, rather than observing actual market behaviour.".

Revealed preference methods infer the money values a monetary benefit valuation applies from market choices. HEAO defines monetary benefit valuation as "A valuation in which a stated health benefit or other outcome is valued in money as a whole, such as by the willingness to pay elicited by contingent valuation, for use in cost-benefit analysis."; HEO defines Revealed Preference as "An approach to inferring consumer preferences from observed choices in actual markets, rather than from hypothetical survey responses.".

Value transfer reuses a money value in a new context, a change of valuation context that HEAO records. HEAO defines monetary value of health as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of health or of risk reduction, used to convert health into money or money into health."; HEO defines Value Transfer as "The general practice of applying an economic value estimated in one context to a decision in a different context.".

Unit value transfer applies one mean money value unchanged in a new context. HEAO defines monetary value of health as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of health or of risk reduction, used to convert health into money or money into health."; HEO defines Unit Value Transfer as "The simplest form of benefit transfer, applying a single mean value from an original study directly to a new context without adjustment.".

Opportunity cost analysis estimates the health forgone elsewhere in a system; the HEAO valuation is the step that converts a cost into that health. HEAO defines health opportunity cost valuation as "A health-money exchange in which a cost falling on a constrained health budget is converted into the health expected to be forgone elsewhere in that system, by dividing it by a money value of a QALY taken to reflect the marginal productivity of the budget, either an estimated supply-side threshold value or a value a decision-making body has adopted for that purpose."; HEO defines Opportunity Cost Analysis as "A form of analysis explicitly estimating the health or value forgone elsewhere in a system when resources are allocated to a specific intervention.".

International reference pricing sets a price by rule from prices in a basket of countries, recorded as a RHEO international reference pricing rule. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines International Reference Pricing as "A pricing policy setting a country's drug price with explicit reference to prices charged for the same product in a defined basket of countries.".

Internal reference pricing sets one reimbursement level for similar drugs, a payer's valuation specification. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Internal Reference Pricing as "A policy grouping therapeutically similar drugs and setting a single reference reimbursement level, requiring patients to pay any difference for pricier options.".

Reference pricing sets a benchmark price, a payer's valuation specification. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Reference Pricing as "A pricing policy setting a benchmark price based on prices of similar products or the same product elsewhere, constraining pharmaceutical spending.".

A fee schedule lists the amounts a payer pays for each service, a payer's valuation specification. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Fee Schedule as "A comprehensive list specifying the predetermined payment amount a payer will reimburse for each specific service, organised by standardised procedure codes.".

Payment rate setting is how a payer fixes the amounts that the administered price method applies. HEAO defines administered price method as "A valuation method in which a resource or a care process is valued at the amount a payer has set for it in a tariff, a fee schedule or a price agreement, which may differ from both its market price and its opportunity cost."; HEO defines Payment Rate Setting as "The process by which a payer determines reimbursement for a service or payment category, incorporating resource cost, market rates, and policy goals.".

Payment by Results paid NHS hospitals by tariff, a payer's valuation specification. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Payment by Results as "Payment by Results was England's tariff-based system for paying NHS hospitals for activity, replaced by the National Tariff Payment System in 2014/15.".

A relative value scale gives the structure of a fee schedule that the administered price method applies. HEAO defines administered price method as "A valuation method in which a resource or a care process is valued at the amount a payer has set for it in a tariff, a fee schedule or a price agreement, which may differ from both its market price and its opportunity cost."; HEO defines Relative Value Scale as "A system assigning a numerical value to each service reflecting its relative resource intensity, providing the structure for a standardised fee schedule.".

A healthcare resource group is the NHS case group to which a tariff assigns an amount, as a diagnosis related group is elsewhere. HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to."; HEO defines Healthcare Resource Group as "A patient classification system used within the NHS grouping clinically similar treatments expected to use similar resources, analogous to diagnosis related groups elsewhere.".

A reference cost is a standardised unit cost of a service, a unit cost weight on an accounting cost basis. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Reference Cost as "A standardised unit cost for a specific healthcare service, published by a health system to promote consistency in costing across providers.".

The national schedule lists average unit costs of NHS services, a source of unit cost weights. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines National Schedule of Reference Costs as "The National Schedule of Reference Costs listed average unit costs of NHS services in England, renamed the National Schedule of NHS Costs from 2018/19.".

A confidential discount lowers the net price a unit cost weight records. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Confidential Discount as "A price reduction negotiated privately between a manufacturer and payer, keeping a higher public list price while offering a lower net price.".

A confidential price is a net price, the amount a unit cost weight may record without publishing it. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Confidential Price as "The actual net price paid for a treatment following a confidential discount, differing from and typically lower than the publicly disclosed list price.".

A launch price is a list price that can be the basis of a unit cost weight. HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost."; HEO defines Launch Price as "The initial price at which a manufacturer introduces a new drug to a specific market, shaping both initial access and later reference pricing.".

The nested Monte Carlo EVPPI method runs an inner simulation within each outer draw, a nested loop. HEAO defines nested Monte Carlo EVPPI method as "A value of information calculation method in which the EVPPI of a subset of parameters is estimated by an outer sample of those parameters and an inner sample of the remaining parameters for each outer draw."; HEO defines Nested Loop as "A simulation structure in which one inner simulation runs repeatedly within each iteration of an outer simulation, used to separate sources of uncertainty.".

The inner loop samples the remaining parameters for each outer draw of the nested EVPPI method. HEAO defines nested Monte Carlo EVPPI method as "A value of information calculation method in which the EVPPI of a subset of parameters is estimated by an outer sample of those parameters and an inner sample of the remaining parameters for each outer draw."; HEO defines Inner Loop as "The portion of a nested simulation running a complete analysis for each parameter set drawn in an outer loop, used in value of information calculations.".

The outer loop samples the parameters of interest in the nested EVPPI method. HEAO defines nested Monte Carlo EVPPI method as "A value of information calculation method in which the EVPPI of a subset of parameters is estimated by an outer sample of those parameters and an inner sample of the remaining parameters for each outer draw."; HEO defines Outer Loop as "The portion of a nested simulation sampling parameter values that remain fixed while a complete inner loop simulation runs beneath it.".

Gaussian process regression is one of the regressions used to estimate EVPPI from a single probabilistic sample. HEAO defines regression-based EVPPI method as "A value of information calculation method in which the EVPPI of a subset of parameters is estimated from a single probabilistic sensitivity analysis sample by regressing net benefit on those parameters with a nonparametric regression."; HEO defines Gaussian Process Regression as "Gaussian process regression is a probabilistic method that predicts an unknown function from observed input-output pairs by conditioning a joint Gaussian model specified through a mean and covariance function.".

EVIC is a value of information measure that weighs further evidence against its cost. HEAO defines value of information analysis as "A valuation in which the expected value of reducing decision uncertainty is assigned, as the expected gain in net benefit from deciding with more information, calculated from a probabilistic analysis at a stated money value of health."; HEO defines EVIC as "A value of information measure expressing the expected value of collecting further evidence before a technology decision, weighed against its cost.".

Adaptive value of information applies value of information analysis at each stage of staged research. HEAO defines value of information analysis as "A valuation in which the expected value of reducing decision uncertainty is assigned, as the expected gain in net benefit from deciding with more information, calculated from a probabilistic analysis at a stated money value of health."; HEO defines Adaptive Value of Information as "Adaptive value of information applies VOI analysis to staged research, re-valuing further data at each interim look to decide whether to continue.".

Research prioritisation uses value of information analysis to decide which research to fund. HEAO defines value of information analysis as "A valuation in which the expected value of reducing decision uncertainty is assigned, as the expected gain in net benefit from deciding with more information, calculated from a probabilistic analysis at a stated money value of health."; HEO defines Research Prioritisation as "The process of deciding which research studies to fund first, given limited resources, informed by formal value of information methods.".

A disease severity classification sorts conditions into the bands a severity weighting rule weights. HEAO defines severity weighting rule as "An equity weighting rule that sets the weight given to QALYs by bands of absolute and proportional QALY shortfall, applying whichever implies the greater severity."; HEO defines Disease Severity Classification as "A formal system categorising disease severity, used within some assessment frameworks to apply differential weighting or thresholds accordingly.".

Severity of disease is what a severity weighting rule measures, for NICE by QALY shortfall. HEAO defines severity weighting rule as "An equity weighting rule that sets the weight given to QALYs by bands of absolute and proportional QALY shortfall, applying whichever implies the greater severity."; HEO defines Severity of Disease as "A measure of how serious a condition is, assessed by factors such as expected mortality or reduction in quality-adjusted life expectancy if untreated.".

The threshold approach compares an ICER with a predetermined money value of a QALY. HEAO defines money value of a QALY as "A monetary value of health that is an amount of money per QALY, used as the exchange rate between health and money in net benefit and in comparison with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio."; HEO defines Threshold Approach as "A decision-making method that classifies an intervention as cost-effective or not based on whether its ICER falls below a predetermined threshold.".

ASCOT is a preference-weighted measure whose preference weights are a weight function anchored on dead. HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed."; HEO defines ASCOT as "ASCOT is the Adult Social Care Outcomes Toolkit, a preference-weighted measure of social care-related quality of life for economic evaluation of care.".

ICECAP-A responses are scored on UK index values by capability index scoring. HEAO defines capability index scoring as "A health state scoring in which a person's responses to a capability instrument, such as the ICECAP-A, are converted into a capability index value by applying a capability or care-related index value set, on a scale anchored at no capability and full capability."; HEO defines ICECAP-A as "ICECAP-A is a self-report capability wellbeing measure for adults, with five attributes scored on UK index values, for economic evaluation beyond health.".

ICECAP-O responses are scored on UK index values by capability index scoring. HEAO defines capability index scoring as "A health state scoring in which a person's responses to a capability instrument, such as the ICECAP-A, are converted into a capability index value by applying a capability or care-related index value set, on a scale anchored at no capability and full capability."; HEO defines ICECAP-O as "ICECAP-O is a five-attribute capability wellbeing measure for people aged 65 and over, with UK index values for evaluating health and social care.".

An informal care cost is the result of an informal care valuation, by replacement cost or forgone time. HEAO defines informal care valuation as "A resource valuation in which the time informal carers spend giving care is converted into money, by the proxy good method, the opportunity cost method, contingent valuation or the well-being valuation method."; HEO defines Informal Care Cost as "The economic value of unpaid caregiving time from family or friends, typically estimated using replacement cost or the carer's forgone time.".

Multi-criteria decision analysis combines scores on several criteria with judged weights, which the weighted sum valuation does. HEAO defines MCDA weighted sum valuation as "A valuation in which the scores of an option on several criteria are combined into one overall value by weighting each score by its MCDA criterion weight and summing, as in the additive model of multi-criteria decision analysis."; HEO defines Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis as "Multi-criteria decision analysis is a family of structured methods that compares alternatives across multiple explicit criteria and incorporates judgments about the trade-offs among them.".

MCDA in HTA appraises technologies on weighted criteria, by a weighted sum valuation. HEAO defines MCDA weighted sum valuation as "A valuation in which the scores of an option on several criteria are combined into one overall value by weighting each score by its MCDA criterion weight and summing, as in the additive model of multi-criteria decision analysis."; HEO defines MCDA in HTA as "MCDA in HTA uses multi-criteria decision analysis to appraise health technologies on explicit, often weighted, criteria such as health gain and severity.".

ENBS calculation is the process that gives an ENBS estimate. HEAO defines ENBS estimate as "A value of information estimate equal to the population EVSI of a proposed study minus the expected cost of the study, which is maximised over sample sizes and allocations to choose the design of further research."; HEO defines ENBS Calculation as "The process of computing the expected net benefit of sampling, the expected value of sample information from a study minus its expected cost.".

The fair innings argument gives priority to people who die young, a basis for equity weights. HEAO defines equity weight as "A decision modifier QALY weight applied according to the group, condition or circumstance of the people who gain or lose, expressing a social value judgement about distribution rather than an individual's preference for a health state."; HEO defines Fair Innings as "An ethical argument holding that people who die young have been deprived of a fair share of a normal lifespan, deserving greater priority.".

Presenteeism is reduced output at work, one of the losses a productivity cost valuation values. HEAO defines productivity cost valuation as "A resource valuation in which time lost from paid or unpaid productive activity, or reduced output at work, because of ill health or premature death is converted into money, by the human capital method or the friction cost method."; HEO defines Presenteeism as "Reduced productivity from an employee who is physically present at work but performing below their normal capacity due to illness or injury.".

Productivity value is the effect of a technology on ability to work, which a productivity cost valuation puts in money. HEAO defines productivity cost valuation as "A resource valuation in which time lost from paid or unpaid productive activity, or reduced output at work, because of ill health or premature death is converted into money, by the human capital method or the friction cost method."; HEO defines Productivity Value as "A component of a technology's value reflecting its effect on a patient's ability to work and contribute economically, beyond clinical improvement.".

Wellbeing, measured as life satisfaction, is what a wellbeing-adjusted time valuation counts in WELLBYs. HEAO defines wellbeing-adjusted time valuation as "A valuation in which a change in life satisfaction, measured on a 0 to 10 scale, is converted into wellbeing-adjusted life years (WELLBYs), one WELLBY being a one-point change in life satisfaction for one person for one year."; HEO defines Wellbeing as "A broad concept covering an individual's overall state of comfort, health, and happiness, of which health-related quality of life is one part.".

A utility estimate is a preference-based utility weight when a valuation applies it, but not every utility estimate is applied, so no subclass axiom is asserted. HEAO defines preference-based utility weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the preference for a health state on a scale on which full health is 1 and dead is 0, with values below 0 for states worse than dead, used to weight time lived in that state."; RHEO defines utility estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the preference-based value of a health state on a scale on which full health is 1 and dead is 0, obtained by a stated valuation method and, for indirect methods, a stated instrument and value set.".

A monetary valuation estimate can be a money amount for a whole benefit, the result of a monetary benefit valuation, so it is not bridged under monetary value of health. HEAO defines monetary benefit valuation as "A valuation in which a stated health benefit or other outcome is valued in money as a whole, such as by the willingness to pay elicited by contingent valuation, for use in cost-benefit analysis."; OHEO defines monetary valuation estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate that expresses the value of a health outcome or a change in risk in money, obtained from stated or revealed preferences.".

Utility mapping predicts a utility from another instrument. Whether that is a valuation is open for Darrin Baines, so no bridge axiom is asserted in 0.1.0. HEAO defines health state scoring as "A valuation in which a health state description, or a person's responses to an instrument, is given a weight on a weight scale, such as a preference-based utility or a capability index value, by applying a weight function."; OHEO defines utility mapping process as "A health state valuation process in which utilities are predicted from responses to another instrument by applying a mapping function.".

A value set coefficient may be a level decrement, but also a constant, an interaction term or a multiplicative utility, so OHEO's preference weight is bridged directly under valuation weight instead. HEAO defines utility decrement as "A valuation weight that is a reduction in preference-based utility associated with an event, a treatment or a health state, applied by subtraction from a baseline utility."; OHEO defines preference weight as "An information content entity that is a number in a value set giving the change in utility associated with one level of one dimension, or with an interaction between levels.".

A utility function assigns a number to each health state or outcome, and a value set assigns a utility to every state of a classification system, so both are weight functions. OHEO keeps the identifiers and says how they were obtained. OHEO defines utility function as "An information content entity that represents preferences over health states or health outcomes by assigning a number to each, so that more preferred states have higher numbers."; HEAO defines weight function as "An information content entity that assigns a valuation weight to each member of a set of descriptions, such as a value set that assigns a utility to every health state of a classification system, so that the weight for any described case can be looked up or computed.".

A QALY calculation turns time in health states into QALYs by utility weights, which is health-adjusted time valuation. RHEO defines QALY calculation process as "A planned process in which quality-adjusted life years are calculated from utility values and the time over which they apply, with or without discounting."; HEAO defines health-adjusted time valuation as "A valuation in which time lived, or time spent in a health state, is converted into health-adjusted time on a health value scale, such as QALYs or DALYs, by applying a preference-based utility weight or a disability weight to each period.".

A DALY calculation turns time lived with disability and life lost into DALYs by disability weights and a standard life expectancy, which is health-adjusted time valuation. OHEO defines DALY calculation process as "A planned process in which disability-adjusted life years are calculated as years of life lost plus years lived with disability."; HEAO defines health-adjusted time valuation as "A valuation in which time lived, or time spent in a health state, is converted into health-adjusted time on a health value scale, such as QALYs or DALYs, by applying a preference-based utility weight or a disability weight to each period.".

Indirect health state valuation applies an existing value set to a person's responses without eliciting new preferences, so it applies a weight function and is preference-based index scoring. OHEO also places it under preference elicitation, and moving it out is proposed for OHEO 0.2.1. OHEO defines indirect health state valuation process as "A health state valuation process in which a person's responses to a preference-based measure are converted to a utility using an existing value set, without the person valuing states themselves."; HEAO defines preference-based index scoring as "A health state scoring in which a person's health state profile on a preference-based measure is converted into a single utility by applying a value set, without the person valuing health states themselves.".

A unit cost valuation multiplies a resource use quantity by a unit cost, the canonical resource valuation. RHEO defines unit cost valuation process as "A costing process in which the quantity of each recorded resource use, or of a recorded absence from work, is multiplied by a stated unit cost, producing one cost record for each record valued."; HEAO defines resource valuation as "A valuation in which a quantity of resource use, or of time, is converted into money by applying a unit cost or price, or by a statistical or accounting costing method.".

A cost estimation process estimates a cost by a statistical or accounting method. It may start from amounts already in money, as a regression of costs does, so it is bridged to valuation only, as cost adjustment is. RHEO defines cost estimation process as "A costing process in which a cost is estimated by a statistical or accounting method rather than by multiplying one quantity by one unit cost, such as a regression of costs on patient characteristics, or an activity-based or step-down allocation of a budget to activities."; HEAO defines valuation as "A planned process in which a value on a stated value scale is assigned to a quantity, or to a valuation target, by applying a valuation weight, a weight function or a valuation function under a stated valuation specification, so that the quantity is expressed as health value, money or another value used in health economic evaluation.".

A cost adjustment converts, inflates, deflates or discounts a cost record by a stated factor, so it is a valuation. Its kind decides whether it is a monetary revaluation or a time valuation, so it is bridged to valuation only. RHEO defines cost adjustment process as "A costing process in which a cost record is converted to another currency, inflated or deflated to another price year, or discounted to a base year, using a stated factor."; HEAO defines valuation as "A planned process in which a value on a stated value scale is assigned to a quantity, or to a valuation target, by applying a valuation weight, a weight function or a valuation function under a stated valuation specification, so that the quantity is expressed as health value, money or another value used in health economic evaluation.".

A discounting specification states the discount rates and base year, the judgement a time valuation applies. RHEO defines discounting specification as "A directive information entity stating the annual discount rates for costs and for health outcomes and the base year to which future values are discounted."; HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to.".

A decision threshold specification states the value of health in money against which results are judged, a decision maker's valuation judgement. RHEO defines decision threshold specification as "A directive information entity stating a value against which a decision maker compares the results of an economic evaluation, such as a cost-effectiveness threshold per QALY gained."; HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to.".

A tariff states the amount a payer pays for a kind of care, a payer's valuation of that care, which may differ from its cost. RHEO defines tariff as "A directive information entity, issued by an organization, that sets the amount to be paid for a stated kind of care process in a stated period, such as a national price for an emergency admission."; HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to.".

A price agreement states the price a payer pays for a technology, a payer's valuation of it. RHEO defines price agreement as "A directive information entity recording the price a payer pays for a health technology, such as a list price, a confidential discount or a managed access agreement, and the period it applies to."; HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to.".

An international reference pricing rule states how a payer values a technology from prices elsewhere. RHEO defines international reference pricing rule as "A directive information entity stating the countries whose prices are referenced, how those prices are adjusted and which of them sets the price benchmark for a health technology, such as the second-lowest GDP-adjusted net price in a basket of countries."; HEAO defines valuation specification as "A directive information entity stating the value judgement a valuation is to apply, such as a discount rate, equity weights for groups or conditions, a money value of health or the prices and tariffs to use, so that the judgement can be identified, attributed and contested apart from the quantities it is applied to.".

A disability weight estimate rates health loss in a state on the scale on which full health is 0 and death is 1, the weight a DALY calculation applies. RHEO defines disability weight estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the severity of a health state on a scale on which 0 is full health and 1 is equivalent to death, used to calculate years lived with disability."; HEAO defines disability weight as "A valuation weight that expresses the loss of health in a health state on a scale on which 0 is full health and 1 is equivalent to death, used to weight time lived with disability in DALYs.".

A unit cost estimate is money per unit of a resource or care process, the weight a resource valuation applies to a quantity. RHEO defines unit cost estimate as "A cost estimate for one unit of a resource or of a health care process, such as one hospital bed day or one consultation."; HEAO defines unit cost or price weight as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of a resource or a care process, in a stated currency and price year, on a stated price basis such as market price, administered price or opportunity cost, and as an average or a marginal cost.".

A currency conversion estimate is the rate at which amounts convert between currencies or price years, a monetary adjustment factor. RHEO defines currency conversion estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the rate at which amounts in one currency or price year convert to another, such as an exchange rate or a purchasing power parity conversion factor."; HEAO defines monetary adjustment factor as "A valuation weight that is a ratio converting an amount of money from one price year or currency to another, such as a price index ratio, a market exchange rate or a purchasing power parity conversion factor.".

column2: value of a statistical life estimate
column22: A value of a statistical life estimate is an amount of money per expected death prevented, a monetary value per unit of risk reduction. OHEO defines value of a statistical life estimate as "A monetary valuation estimate of the aggregate willingness to pay for mortality risk reductions that together prevent one expected death."; HEAO defines monetary value of health as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of health or of risk reduction, used to convert health into money or money into health.".

column2: value of a statistical life year estimate
column22: A value of a statistical life year estimate is an amount of money per statistical life year, a monetary value per unit of health. OHEO defines value of a statistical life year estimate as "A monetary valuation estimate of the value of one statistical life year, derived from willingness to pay for reductions in mortality risk."; HEAO defines monetary value of health as "A valuation weight that is an amount of money per unit of health or of risk reduction, used to convert health into money or money into health.".

A utility decrement estimate is a loss of utility for an event, a treatment or a state relative to a baseline, applied by subtraction. OHEO defines utility decrement estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the loss of utility associated with an event, a treatment or a health state, relative to a stated baseline."; HEAO defines utility decrement as "A valuation weight that is a reduction in preference-based utility associated with an event, a treatment or a health state, applied by subtraction from a baseline utility.".

A preference weight is a number in a value set giving the change in utility for one level of one dimension or for an interaction, a coefficient the value set combines into a utility, so it is a valuation weight. It is not bridged under utility decrement, because not every coefficient is subtracted from a baseline, and OHEO already names it value set coefficient as a synonym, so HEAO adds no class of its own. OHEO defines preference weight as "An information content entity that is a number in a value set giving the change in utility associated with one level of one dimension, or with an interaction between levels."; HEAO defines valuation weight as "An information content entity that is a number applied in a valuation to convert a quantity into value, such as a utility, a unit cost, a discount factor, a money value of a QALY or an equity weight, stated with the value scale it converts to.".

RHEO's perspective specification is the analytic perspective, whose costs and outcomes a study counts. The valuation perspective is whose values supply the weights. Darrin Baines asked for the two to be kept apart. RHEO defines perspective specification as "A directive information entity stating whose resources and outcomes an economic evaluation counts, such as the health and personal social services system or society as a whole, by listing the kinds of resource included."; HEAO defines valuation perspective as "A directive information entity stating whose values supply the weights a valuation applies, such as the preferences of a general population or of patients, the prices a payer pays, or the social value judgements of a decision-making body.".

RHEO links a cost record to the resource use record it values; HEAO links the valuation itself to its quantity, so the two differ in domain and are not sub-properties. HEAO defines has valued quantity as "Relates a valuation to the information content entity recording the quantity it values, such as a resource use record, a time in a health state or an amount already valued."; RHEO defines values resource use as "Relates a cost record to the resource use record or work absence record it values.".

RHEO links a cost record to the unit cost it applies; HEAO links the valuation to every kind of weight it applies. HEAO defines applies weight as "Relates a valuation to a valuation weight it applies to its valued quantity, such as a unit cost, a utility, a discount factor, a money value of a QALY or an equity weight."; RHEO defines uses unit cost as "Relates a cost record to the unit cost estimate it applies.".

RHEO links an adjusted cost record to its adjustment factor; HEAO links the revaluation or time valuation to that factor. HEAO defines applies weight as "Relates a valuation to a valuation weight it applies to its valued quantity, such as a unit cost, a utility, a discount factor, a money value of a QALY or an equity weight."; RHEO defines uses adjustment factor as "Relates an adjusted cost record to the estimate it applies, such as an exchange rate, a price index ratio or a discount factor.".

RHEO links a discounted cost record to its discounting specification; HEAO links the time valuation to it. HEAO defines follows valuation specification as "Relates a valuation to the valuation specification that states the judgement it applies, such as a discounting specification, a decision threshold specification, a tariff or a severity weighting rule. It shortens the OBI chain in which a planned process realises a plan that concretizes a directive information entity."; RHEO defines uses discounting specification as "Relates a discounted cost record to the discounting specification (rates and base year) it applies.".

RHEO links an adjusted cost record to the record it adjusts; in HEAO that earlier cost record is the valued quantity of the monetary revaluation or time valuation, so the two properties meet through the valuation. HEAO defines has valued quantity as "Relates a valuation to the information content entity recording the quantity it values, such as a resource use record, a time in a health state or an amount already valued."; RHEO defines adjusts cost record as "Relates an adjusted cost record to the cost record it converts, inflates, deflates or discounts.".

OHEO links a utility record to the value set it was obtained with; in HEAO the utility is a weight derived by the index scoring that applied that value set. HEAO defines weight derived by as "Relates a valuation weight to what produced its value, such as the valuation that applied a value set to a profile, a preference elicitation process or a value set development study."; OHEO defines obtained with value set as "Relates a RHEO utility measurement record or utility estimate to the value set used to convert instrument responses to utilities. The value is an instance of a named value set class: one release of that value set.".

RHEO keeps the value set as text on a utility record; HEAO links the weight to what produced it by identifier. HEAO defines weight derived by as "Relates a valuation weight to what produced its value, such as the valuation that applied a value set to a profile, a preference elicitation process or a value set development study."; RHEO defines has value set as "The value set (tariff) used to turn an instrument's health state descriptions into utilities, such as the UK value set, without the instrument or its version, which are given by has instrument and has instrument version.".

RHEO keeps the health state valuation method as text; HEAO links a valuation to a valuation method by identifier. HEAO defines uses valuation method as "Relates a valuation, a valuation weight or a weight function to the valuation method by which it values or was made to value."; RHEO defines has valuation method as "The method used to value a health state: indirect (an instrument with a value set) or direct, such as time trade-off or standard gamble.".

OHEO links a value set to the kind of elicitation that derived it; HEAO links a valuation or weight function to how values are applied. HEAO defines uses valuation method as "Relates a valuation, a valuation weight or a weight function to the valuation method by which it values or was made to value."; OHEO defines value set elicited by as "Relates a value set or an index value set to the kind of preference elicitation process by which the preferences it rests on were elicited, such as composite time trade-off. Named so as not to be confused with the RHEO datatype property has valuation method (RHEO_2000023).".

OHEO describes the population whose preferences produced a value set in free text; HEAO links a weight function to a preference source specification. HEAO defines from valuation perspective as "Relates a valuation, a valuation weight or a weight function to the valuation perspective stating whose values supply its weight."; OHEO defines has valuation population as "A description of the population whose preferences were elicited to produce a value set.".

RHEO links a utility estimate to the health state it values; HEAO links any valuation to the entity its value is about. HEAO defines has valuation target as "Relates a valuation to the entity its value is about, such as a health state, a kind of resource, a group of patients or a decision."; RHEO defines values health state as "Relates a utility estimate or an assumed utility to the health state description it values. A utility measured in people values a clinical or classification state description, not a model state.".

RHEO links a costing process or cost record to an assumption its valuation rests on; HEAO records the provenance of every valuation. HEAO defines has valuation provenance as "Relates a valuation, a valuation weight, a weight function or a valuation specification to the valuation provenance record of who made or adopted it, from which source and when."; RHEO defines valuation rests on assumption as "Relates a costing process or a cost record to a modelling assumption its valuation depends on, such as the choice of a replacement cost for informal care.".

RHEO links an opportunity cost record to the alternative use forgone; HEAO links the cost record of the spending to the health opportunity cost record computed from it. HEAO defines has health opportunity cost as "Relates a cost record of spending that falls on a constrained health budget to the opportunity cost record of the health expected to be forgone elsewhere in that system because of it."; RHEO defines forgoes alternative as "Relates an opportunity cost record to the alternative use of the resource that was forgone, given as an intervention specification or a care process type specification.".
